payload.goal: Make sofar measurably the best work memory for AI coding agents: never below any agent's native memory on any rep, bookkeeping at or below native overhead, and a lead of at least 25-30% (target 2x) on held-out long-horizon, cross-agent, decision-churn work. The lead must survive a native memory that syncs across machines and teammates, so it may never rest on native memory being machine-local.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Wave A: parity at native overhead (ships in 0.33.0-rc.2)

tasks.title: A1 overhead cut: adopt the session from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (start_session becomes a fallback), load sofar MCP tools up front (no ToolSearch), a batched end_session taking decisions[]/tasks[]/notes[], task status derived from commits and tests instead of per-subtask update_task. PREDICT (chain A, prompt-matched pairs): store share ≤12% of tool calls on every rep; sofar/automemory cost ≤0.9; retention within ±1 decision. Contract Decisions first (SPEC start_session and end_session).

A2 rule fidelity: a rule stores the operator's quote beside it, the digest renders the quote, and a warning fires when a rule adds status codes, paths or values the quote lacks. PREDICT: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.

A3 digest composition: next task's spec first; remember entries surfaced; implementation minutiae dropped from rejected approaches and recent decisions; rules ranked by relevance and rendered last; ≤6k chars. PREDICT: ≤1 raw .sofar read per session; M3 unchanged or better.
rust-core mirrors 1.1–1.3 (hooks, digest render) with conformance parity before rc.2 is pinned

B1 read-time surfacing: when a file is read or edited, the decisions whose guard or derived scope matches it are shown, worded as facts (Claude PostToolUse on Read/Grep, Codex Bash/apply_patch, Cursor postToolUse). PREDICT: C3 re-violation −50%, tokens +<1%.

B2 repo-wide scope and supersession across initiatives: a rule can be app-wide; a reversal of a standing rule in ANY initiative is refused without supersedes (extends L08, which is same-record only). Fixes cursor-sofar's cross-record A2 loss.
B3 executable decision checks with fix hints in the failure, run at Stop, pre-commit and in drive. Blocking needs a Decision revisiting drift-hardening D3 (warn, never block) first.
B4 optional bridge into native memory (repo-local autoMemoryDirectory import, Codex summary), user/feedback types kept local. Needs a privacy Decision first.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Wave C: scale (Rust core, cloud)

Read-time hook under 20 ms at 50+ initiatives and team100 scale (Rust core)

phases.name: Phase 4 — Moat against a cloud-synced native memory

tasks.title: Moat spec: assume Claude Code (and others) ship shared cloud memory; list the advantages that survive: vendor-neutral cross-agent memory, branch- and PR-aware records that merge with the code, typed decisions with supersession and provenance to commits and tests, executable enforcement, deterministic zero-model capture, team governance of rules. Each maps to a benchmark claim with a falsifier.
Retire any public claim or roadmap item whose advantage rests only on native memory being machine-local

Chain L design and budget: ~30 sessions, ~24 planted decisions (guarded, superseded once or twice, why-only), segments across Claude, Codex, fresh clone, concurrent worktrees and a forced compaction. Arms MUST include a native-memory-SYNCED arm (memory dir carried across machines, clones and teammates; Codex idle gate 0) standing in for future cloud memory. Scoped to the D17 cap before authoring.
Author Chain L, hidden tests and a sealed reference by an author blind to fix-building; mutation-validate every planted decision
Round-3 pre-registration frozen with lead predictions (≥25–30%, target 2×) against the synced native arm
Run round 3, report per claim with per-rep values; publish only what clears the pre-registered margin

payload.because: A vendor can remove the machine-local limit with one release. The lasting lead has to come from what a single-vendor, free-form, model-curated memory structurally lacks: memory shared across agents, records that follow git branches and merges, decisions with supersession and provenance, executable enforcement, zero-model capture, and team governance.

payload.because: Round 1's only Claude quality miss was lost at capture. The operator said "Reject anything else"; the agent's rule added "with 4xx"; the "obey verbatim" header made that paraphrase law, so S9 returned 400 and failed A6. Keeping the operator's words beside the rule, and flagging what the rule adds in every digest, puts the source in front of each later session at zero extra calls. The write-time warning lets the capturing session correct the rule the moment it logs it. Frozen prediction: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.
payload.chose: 1.2 CONTRACT (rule fidelity). (a) decision_logged gains `quote?`: the operator's own words the rule came from, copied exactly, non-empty, at most 300 chars, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). (b) A pure core/rule-fidelity.ts lists a rule's SPECIFICS: HTTP status codes and classes (400, 4xx), paths (a token with `/` between word characters, or a file name with an extension), and values (backticked spans, double-quoted spans, tokens carrying a digit). It then reports the specifics the quote lacks, by case-insensitive whitespace-collapsed substring. (c) Standing constraints renders each quoted rule as `- [D<n>] <rule> — operator: "<quote>"`, plus ` (not in the operator's words: <specifics>)` when any are missing. The header becomes `Standing constraints — obey verbatim; where a rule quotes the operator, the quote decides (<N>):` ONLY when an in-force rule carries a quote, so quote-less records render byte-identically. decisions.md and the review packet render the quote too. (d) sofar_log_decision returns `warnings[]`, and `sofar event append --type decision_logged` prints them, naming the unquoted specifics; never a refusal. (e) The `rule` and `quote` descriptions and the CLI dialect's fields teach: word the rule as the operator did, and pass their words as quote. Guard notices in hooks are unchanged in 1.2.
payload.over: Refusing a rule that adds specifics (a paraphrase that rightly names a file would cost a retry, and the plan says warn); recording prompts so the quote can be verified mechanically (user content in the record); rendering the quote instead of the rule (the operator's sentence often lacks the context the rule supplies); clipping long quotes at render (a clipped quote can drop the clause that matters, so the cap sits at validation)

A `rule` is the agent's restatement of what the operator said, and a
restatement can add law nobody made (round 1: "Reject anything else" became
"…reject anything else with 4xx", and S9 obeyed the 4xx). `quote` carries the

SPECIFICS of a rule, in rule order, deduplicated case-insensitively:
backticked, straight double-quoted and curly double-quoted spans first, each
one `value` holding its whitespace-collapsed inner text. The text between
spans splits on whitespace; each token loses leading `( [ { < ' " ‘ “` and
trailing `) ] } > ' " ’ ” , ; : . ! ?`, then classifies by the first match:
`status` — `^([1-5][0-9]{2}|[1-5]xx)$` (case-insensitive); `path` — a `/`
with `[\\w.~-]` before and `[\\w.*-]` after, a leading `/` followed by

a specific. A specific is UNQUOTED when its lowercased text does not occur in
the lowercased, whitespace-collapsed quote at a term boundary: where the
specific starts (ends) with `[A-Za-z0-9]`, the quote character before (after)
the occurrence must not be one.

constraints, decisions.md, the review packet): a rule with a quote renders
